## How it works

- [statement] Over short intervals the mid-price change is roughly linear in OFI, and the fit is contemporaneous (same interval), not a forecast. Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov regress mid-price change on OFI over 10-second intervals for 50 US stocks (NYSE TAQ). Xu, Gould and Howison fit a linear model of contemporaneous mid-price change on multi-level OFI for 6 Nasdaq stocks. Bugaenko, in equity data, reports that price impact grows linearly with order-flow imbalance for small signed order flows. (high confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1011.6402 · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06230, https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.08290
- [statement] Coinbase warns that messages can be dropped from the matches channel and recommends tracking the last trade ID through the heartbeat channel and fetching missed trades from REST. Inference, not stated by Coinbase: because CVD is a running sum, an unrepaired gap leaves a permanent offset in every later CVD value. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance
- [statement] Imbalance carries more information when the tick is large relative to price. Gould and Bonart report considerable improvement in direction classification for large-tick stocks and only moderate improvement for small-tick stocks. Bieganowski and Slepaczuk report that the predictive effect of imbalance (SHAP) is stronger for instruments with larger ticks. Implication to test: expect a cleaner OBI signal on coarse-tick pairs than on very fine-tick ones. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492 · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.00776

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Input representation matters more than model depth. Kolm et al. find models trained on order flow (stationary inputs derived from the book) significantly outperform most models trained directly on raw order book states (115 Nasdaq stocks). Xu et al. find the out-of-sample fit of the contemporaneous OFI relationship improves with each added price level (6 Nasdaq stocks). Wang (Bybit BTC/USDT snapshots at 100 ms to multi-second intervals) reports simpler models can match or beat deeper networks when preprocessing is good. (medium confidence) — https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/mathfi/v33y2023i4p1044-1081.html · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06230, https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05764

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] CVD (cumulative volume delta) is the running sum of per-bar delta, where delta = taker (aggressor) buy volume minus taker sell volume. Only the aggressing side of each trade is counted, so unlike total volume it is signed. Because it is a running sum, its level depends on where the window starts; the change over a window is what carries information. (high confidence) — https://www.coinglass.com/cvd · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance · also: https://studio.glassnode.com/charts/market.SpotCvdSum?a=BNB

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Forward-looking evidence on book imbalance sits at very short horizons. Gould and Bonart predict the direction of the next mid-price move from queue imbalance (10 Nasdaq stocks). Kolm, Turiel and Westray find the effective horizon of stock-specific forecasts is about two average price changes (115 Nasdaq stocks). Bieganowski and Slepaczuk use a 3-second log mid-price return target on 1-second Binance perpetual data. Horizon half-life is owned by a sibling concept; this claim only records the horizons the studies tested. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492 · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance · also: https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/mathfi/v33y2023i4p1044-1081.html, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.00776
- [statement] OFI is computed from best-quote updates. Per book event, e_n = I{P^B_n >= P^B_(n-1)} q^B_n - I{P^B_n <= P^B_(n-1)} q^B_(n-1) - I{P^A_n <= P^A_(n-1)} q^A_n + I{P^A_n >= P^A_(n-1)} q^A_(n-1), where P is the best price, q the best size, B bid, A ask, and I the indicator function. OFI over an interval is the sum of e_n. Multi-level OFI (MLOFI) extends this to a vector over price levels. (medium confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1011.6402 · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06230
- [statement] Venues encode trade direction differently, so a multi-venue CVD must normalise the sign per venue. Binance m says whether the buyer was the maker (true means the taker sold). Coinbase Exchange match messages put the MAKER order side in 'side': 'sell' means the maker sold, the match is an up-tick, and the taker bought. Bybit v5 public trade field S is documented as 'Side of taker'. Treating the three alike flips delta on some venues. (high confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/master/web-socket-streams.md · keywords: Order flow signals CVD and order book imbalance · also: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/channels.md, https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/websocket/public/trade
